question.text: A fund house publishes the following advertisement: "Our Flexi Cap Fund delivered 48% return in the last 8 months! Invest now!" As a SEBI-compliant distributor, you should recognize that this advertisement:

answer.text: Is perfectly compliant as it shows the actual return earned
Should also show the annualized return of 72% for better comparison
Must also include benchmark comparison, returns for standard periods, and a past performance disclaimer
Should convert the 8-month return to CAGR for compliance

explanation.text: The Logic: Cherry-picking the 8-month absolute return (48%) is incomplete and misleading. SEBI's advertisement code for mutual funds requires that performance be presented with benchmark comparison (using TRI), returns for standard periods (1 year, 3 years, 5 years, since inception, as applicable), and the mandatory disclaimer that past performance may or may not be sustained. The Trap: The workbook says schemes existing more than six months but less than one year should provide simple annualized growth rate for the past six months, so a blanket "sub-1-year returns must NEVER be annualized" claim is wrong. For a 6-12 month scheme, the applicable simple annualized six-month disclosure must be made; for schemes older than one year, standard period returns and benchmark comparison apply. Note: Performance advertising for mutual funds is governed by SEBI's advertisement code and AMFI's best practice guidelines. Distributors must verify that any performance material they share carries benchmark comparison, standardized period returns, and the past performance disclaimer.
